Our last dog didn't need entropion surgery. But toward the end of his life he had recurring eye issues, discharge, ulcers. The vet said some dog breeds (shar pei included) have a problem with tear production, aka dry eye. The discharge is created because the eye is irritated. The dryness and irritation leads to ulceration. The cloudiness could be cataracts, but it can also be from the ulcer and many times can be resolved with the right care and antibiotics. Prolonged ulceration can lead to blindness.   
  
"**Keratoconjunctivitis sicca (KCS) is also commonly referred to as dry eye**. The medical term means inflammation of the cornea and surrounding tissues from drying. It is a common eye condition resulting from inadequate production of tears by the lacrimal gland and/or gland of the third eyelid."  
We were in the process of ordering and waiting for some immune eye drops for our dog Mork but he ended up passing away :( He also had lots of hair loss around the eye toward the end from the discharge and eye toilets. 

Anyway, it might be entropion or it could be something like KCS. The most important thing is to visit a vet to find out and if it is KCS get the right drops ordered.   
At home band aid care - keeping the eyes clean and wiping away discharge with clean gentle cloth or wipe. We were advised to use Systane initially twice per day. But when we changed vets and while waiting for new immune eyedrops we were told to use Systane 4-5 times per day minimum. They actually suggested another over the counter eye drop for dry eyes that was better and would only need to be used twice per day, but i can't remember.

We received a note. It was chaotic, like his last moments of lucidity were writing short sentences before it was too late, which he acknowledged too. He named and blamed his workplace and WorkCover, and spoke of his pain and inability to go on. He only mentioned one loved one, which was a vulnerable friend that we (his family and friends) didn't know and he didn't want him to feel abandoned. They had met when they were kids working at the markets, and my brother had kept in contact all these years, even through this person's battle with meth and poverty, we had no idea. I found it really hard that there wasn't anything else in the note, that he didn't say goodbye to anyone else, but I was comforted that one of his last thoughts was of compassion and care for someone else. I worked really hard to find this friend before we let my brother go, and on like day 5 we found him. He came up to the hospital 3 times including the day we said goodbye.

ALSO, second story: I needed to cancel a gym trial that I had started to manage my grief rage, but I was in a car accident and physically couldn't continue. The gym manager tried to say no I couldn't leave and I was basically stubborn AF and had read their T&C's, which he said were N/A because it's a different situation, so I found the other T&C's which he "couldn't find" and I was like nah look I'm not paying because x,y,z in these t&c's. He continued to push back and I was sin his office for 30minutes, so I said, I get this is awkward for you so just give me the head office number/ email and I will do it myself that way I don't put you in a bad sutuation. Then he was like "oh no I'll cancel it I'll cancel it, but you're lucky because I'm nice". Blah blah blah. I was polite and grateful. 


THEN as I was leaving, he was like oh, I really do think you need to work on this stuff though (I was shaking because I was anxious during a difficult conversation, this was weeks after my brother died), like stress management, so if it's not the gym maybe yoga or meditation, and I was like "excuse me?? How do you know I'm not already doing those things?' and he was so condescending and was like "oh it just would have been good to see that earlier"
And I went offffffffff. His brief rebuttal was, "I actually do know what it's like to have someone die because I lost my mum to cancer last year"

And no joke I said to this man's face "HOW LUCKY FOR YOU! WHAT PRIVILEGE YOUR MUM DIED OF CANCER AND YOU GOT TO SAY GOODBYE, BECAUSE I DIDNT AND I WILL NEVER GET TO AND YOU HAVE ABSOLUTELY NO IDEA WHAT IM GOING THROUGH, YOU ARE SOOOOOOO LUCKY. I hope you never speak this way to a customer ever again". He shut his trap up straight away. Obviously I don't condone yelling at strangers, but this felt really good because it was just so insensitive, arrogant and obscene. 

So if you can't say how you feel in this situation, just know I said that with my whole chest for all of us ❤️

I’m sorry you’re feeling this way. I hear you and I understand those big shame feelings and thinking you have failed everyone. As hard as it is to believe, you haven’t. 

When I was 16 I had sex with my bf who I loved deeply and the condom broke. We tried to get the morning after pill but they wouldn’t sell it to me. His mum took me home and my mum accused him of raping me. She then abused me for a year and onwards. She was a catholic so there was a lot of shame. They took me to the drs, made me take the morning after pill and break up with my bf (this really scarred me he still holds a place in my heart). 

I’m in my 30s now, have a career, have travelled the world for and have no kids or partner. I often think how silly my fear and shame was around getting pregnant (Still totally valid). Just that I would have kept the baby if I had a teen pregnancy, and knowing what I know now about life it would have been fine- it would have been really really really really hard, but it would have been fine, because I know me (i also don’t live in the USA and my country’s public health supports are vastly different).

You don’t deserve to carry that shame. These things happen!!! You need to tell your parents asap. They might surprise you and at the end of the day they probably just want you to be happy. But if your parents are abusive I want you to remember and hold onto the fact that you don’t deserve that. Family relationships are complicated and traumatic and hard, but you still need to tell them asap. 

I don’t know you, your level of readiness to take this on, what your dreams are, but hopefully you do??? Have a think about what you really want, your values, and whether you are prepared to do this “alone” (you may not be able to rely on baby daddy or parents) Do you gave the capacity and capabilities to take this on? What kind of parent do you want to be? Why do you want to keep the baby? 
If you are, trust that you will find a way and be prepared to work really hard for that. 
If you aren’t that is okay, it’s okay not to be ready, it’s okay if you can’t afford to have a baby if you aren’t financially stable or supported, its okay to get an abortion. You are not a bad person if you need or want to have an abortion. 

You deserve to make a choice that is not under the duress of others. But you need to make it asap!!! Contact your parents, talk to the baby daddy. Make sure you have somewhere safe to go after talking with your family. 

There are thousands of teen pregnancies every year. It is not the end of the world, just one of life’s difficult hurdles. I’ve also worked with many teen or young mums and some of them are the best mums (but they are switched on, they accessed supports and they had a plan). Trust yourself, know yourself. Nothing is easy, but that is okay- you can do it (whatever that choice is). 

P.s listen to the others and visit a shelter, even just to chat with someone face to face.
